evidence.quote: DA plays a role in decisions about the risk of water loss (74).
In Drosophila, DA regulates foraging behavior in response to hunger and satiation through two distinct dopaminergic circuits (42).
In honey bees, DA acts on neural circuits and receptors associated with both rewarding stimuli and the avoidance of risk.
DA levels in animal brains can change quickly, allowing rapid behavioral adjustment to current conditions (14).
DA release in the nucleus accumbens (NAc), part of the ventral striatum, is particularly important for decisions about whether to engage in risk-taking or risk-averse behavior (27).
